In the mathematical field of [[algebraic geometry]], '''purity''' is a theme covering a number of results and conjectures, which collectively address the question of proving that "when something happens, it happens in a particular [[codimension]]". 

==Purity of the branch locus==
For example, [[Ramification (mathematics)|ramification]] is a phenomenon of codimension 1 (in the geometry of [[complex manifold]]s, reflecting as for [[Riemann surface]]s that ramify at single points that it happens in real codimension two). A classical result, '''Zariski&ndash;Nagata purity''' of [[Masayoshi Nagata]] and [[Oscar Zariski]],<ref>{{cite journal|pmc=534562 | pmid=16590274 | volume=44 | issue=8 |date=August 1958 | journal=Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. | pages=791–6|doi=10.1073/pnas.44.8.791 | title=On the Purity of the Branch Locus of Algebraic Functions | last1=Zariski | first1=O. | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|pmc=534563 | pmid=16590275 | volume=44 | issue=8 |date=August 1958 | journal=Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. | pages=796–9 | doi=10.1073/pnas.44.8.796| title=Remarks on a Paper of Zariski on the Purity of Branch-Loci | last1=Nagata | first1=M. | doi-access=free }}</ref> called also '''purity of the branch locus''', proves that on a non-singular [[algebraic variety]] a ''branch locus'', namely the set of points at which a morphism ramifies, must be made up purely of codimension 1 subvarieties (a [[Weil divisor]]). There have been numerous extensions of this result into theorems of [[commutative algebra]] and [[scheme theory]], establishing purity of the branch locus in the sense of description of the restrictions on the possible "open subsets of failure" to be an [[étale morphism]]. 

==Cohomological purity==
There is also a homological notion of purity that is related, namely a collection of results stating that cohomology groups from a particular theory are trivial with the possible exception of one index ''i''. Such results were established in [[étale cohomology]] by [[Michael Artin]] (included in [[SGA 4]]), and were foundational in setting up the theory to contain expected analogues of results from [[singular cohomology]]. A general statement of [[Alexander Grothendieck]] known as the '''[[absolute cohomological purity conjecture]]''' was proved by Ofer Gabber.<ref>K. Fujiwara, ''A proof of the absolute purity conjecture (after Gabber)''. Algebraic Geometry 2000, Azumino (Hotaka), 153&ndash;183.</ref> It concerns a [[closed immersion]] of schemes (regular, noetherian) that is purely of codimension ''d'', and the relative [[local cohomology]] in the étale theory. With coefficients mod ''n'' where ''n'' is invertible, the cohomology should occur only with index 2''d'' (and take on a predicted value).<ref>As formulated in http://www.math.utah.edu/~niziol/icm20062.pdf, p. 4.</ref>
